author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Whitespace-only queries expose contextual developer slash commands.
findings.consequence: In development, opening Quick Search on a reader or author page and entering only spaces can show /id, /editor, or /info rows even though the visible query is not a command prefix. This is inconsistent with the surrounding QuickSearch row gating, which hides rows for an empty query and only treats slash-prefixed input as command input.
findings.evidence: developerQuickSearchCommands trims the query into normalized on line 176, then filters labels with startsWith(normalized). For a whitespace-only query normalized is "", so every contextual command passes this predicate at line 178. The caller in app/components/global/QuickSearch.vue only checks the raw query for emptiness, so " " reaches developerRows.
findings.recommendation: Return [] when the trimmed query is empty, or make the QuickSearch caller gate on query.value.trim() before asking for developer rows.
